items.heading: Picking Clinical Psychology As Picking
items.text: Picking Clinical Psychology As Picking Clinical Psychology as a "softer" fallback from a failed NEET attempt. The RCI-regulated MA Clinical Psychology route has its own real bottleneck - roughly 10 seats per batch at most universities. Treating it as an easy consolation prize instead of a genuine choice usually means discovering the scarcity problem a second time, several years and a psychology degree later.

rows: Open to any stream - Arts, Commerce, or Science - typically with 50% aggregate in 12th (45% for SC/ST/OBC, varies by university). Your PCB background carries no penalty and no special advantage here; admission usually runs through CUET or a university-specific merit list.

Many universities specifically prefer or require a Science-stream 12th, and several ask for PCB or PCM directly. This is the one Psychology-adjacent degree where your PCB background is not neutral - it is often a stated eligibility requirement, not just a bonus.

BA Psychology leans into culture, personality, social context, and qualitative research. BSc Psychology leans into neuroscience, biological bases of behaviour, cognitive processes, statistics, and lab-based experiments - the exact terrain your PCB Biology and Chemistry already gave you a head start in.

items.heading: Choosing Mbbs
items.text: Choosing MBBS-psychiatry only because "doctor" sounds safer to the family. Psychiatry is one of the least crowded MD specialisations to enter once you clear NEET-PG, but it still sits behind two national exams and roughly 900 seats nationwide. If your real interest is understanding behaviour rather than practising medicine broadly for years first, this is an expensive way to reach a narrower goal.

items.heading: Assuming Every Psychology
items.text: Assuming every psychology-adjacent career needs RCI registration. RCI registration is a legal requirement only for practising as a Clinical Psychologist. Counselling, organisational psychology and HR, behavioural science research, and most academic and teaching roles do not carry this legal step at all.

items.heading: Comparing Psychiatry and Psychology Pay
items.text: Comparing psychiatry and psychology pay using one number from either side. A psychiatrist's average pay and a Clinical Psychologist's government-institute pay are not measuring the same career stage, training length, or legal scope. Compare timeline-to-registration, total training cost, and daily work - not just one salary figure pulled from either side.

items.text: Generic PCB content usually treats psychology as one line item next to nursing and pharmacy, without separating the medical route from the non-medical one.
